comment: Suppresses known-good duplication from check-duplication.mjs. Two matcher forms: `fingerprint` (exact cluster — churns on edit, which deliberately resurfaces the cluster for re-triage) or `files` (every site of the cluster must live in the listed files — for permanent do-not-fix decisions that must survive edits). Optional `signal` narrows a files matcher.

entries.reason: Synthesis verdict: do not fix. The organizer daemon's model-offline backoff (BACKOFF_MIN/MAX ladder) and Breve's restart/lock retry are independently tuned policies for different failure domains; converging them would couple an in-app daemon to a launchd runtime.

Not a mirror: loopback_http.rs owns the status → reason-phrase map for every loopback adapter, and helper.rs is a router that necessarily names the statuses it answers with (204/403/404 …). The shared literals are a caller using its own transport's vocabulary; collapsing them would mean inventing a constant per status code for no behavioural gain. The reading, bearer, refusal-document, and body-bound policy IS shared (loopback_http.rs read_http_head / bearer_authorized / unauthorized / not_found / read_http_body).

Batch 0 independent_security_enforcement: the egress policy is deliberately implemented on both sides of the process boundary and held in parity by scripts/fixtures/egress-fixtures.json — shared literals (private ranges, redirect caps) are the fixture working as designed.
Batch 1 fixture-guarded mirror: endpoint_is_local (chat.rs) vs endpointIsLocal tests share the scripts/fixtures/parity.json endpoint fixture URLs by design.
Fixture-guarded mirror: secret.rs detector tests and loop.test.ts share the same red-team card/SSN vectors; check-secret-parity.mjs holds the two detectors aligned.

TS↔Rust process contract: the themed PDF renderer's argv (--in/--out/--title) is spelled by the script that parses it and by the Rust caller that spawns it; the shared literals are the contract, not copied logic (2026-09-02).
TS↔Rust IPC contract: the five Antigravity action words are spelled once by the command that dispatches them and once by the wrapper that sends them (2026-09-03).

The Antigravity setup card deliberately speaks the AI Models settings vocabulary (.ailane-* rows, .ghostbtn variants, chip states) so it reads as one surface; the shared literals are class names, not copied logic (2026-09-03).

MIRROR-NOT-IMPORT: the Rust search grammar tests and the TS twin's vectors share their literals ON PURPOSE (Groceries/sourdough/Launch checklist…) — the same inputs asserted on both sides of the app/shell boundary are the lockstep proof, not a copy to extract (docs/design/tantivy-search.md).

All are instances of the one small modal grammar (.rename-overlay/.rename-card/.rename-btn, Cancel + primary action) from the design system — the web dialogs share WebDialogFrame; the remaining shared literals are its class names and labels, not copied logic (2026-09-16).
The same Escape-closes-the-card keydown handler the shared dialog grammar prescribes (see web-connect-dialog-shares-rename-card).

MIRROR-NOT-IMPORT: the web's model-facing corpus (services/webAiCorpus.ts) projects the same note-meta field names (folderId, diskFolderId) Rust serialises across the IPC boundary; the shared literals are the wire shape, not copied logic (2026-09-16).

The System browser's folder row moved to its own file (2026-09-16); it and the note rows in systemSurface are the one Finder-column row grammar (.fdr-name/.fdr-date/.fdr-kind), so the shared literals are class names, not copied logic.

Deliberate TS twin of the Rust image magic-number table: Rotli Web has no Rust, so lib/fileKind.ts imageBytesMatchExtension must refuse the same non-images corpus.rs image_payload_matches_extension refuses (a .png that is not a PNG). The literals ARE the contract (GIF87a, RIFF/WEBP, the ftyp brands); the test asserts them so the two cannot drift silently. Same shape as the search_match.rs / TS twin entry.

Deliberate TS twin of the Rust open-task grammar: Rotli Web has no Rust, so lib/taskLines.ts must read and check off exactly the lines corpus.rs open_task_text / check_off do ('[ ]', '[/]', the box found by position). The literals ARE the contract; the test mirrors the Rust cases so the two cannot drift silently. Same shape as the search_match.rs and image-magic twin entries.

The Chat window test asserts the hand-off protocol by its message names ('regroup', 'regrouped'). The literals ARE the contract between the two webviews (docs/architecture/window-events.md rotli:chat-window); a test that did not name them could not prove what the other window receives.

Deliberate TS twin of the Rust board rules: Rotli Web has no Rust, so services/folderBoards.ts must name, place, and collide boards exactly as corpus.rs board_name_stem / create_board_with_stem / free_name do (Project/Map → Project-Map, name-2.excalidraw, storage/excalidraw). The literals ARE the on-disk contract; the test mirrors the Rust cases so the two cannot drift silently. parity.json pins the empty scene and the lane.

Deliberate twin: Rotli Web scaffolds an empty connected folder with the same spine Rust scaffold_memex writes, so the folder opens in Rotli for Mac as a vault it recognizes. The browser cannot call Rust; the shared literals ARE the on-disk contract.

Every setup screen renders the same setup-shell layout (onboarding.css) by class name; the shared literals are the design system's layout vocabulary, not copied logic. Each screen's content and actions differ.
The tests assert the gate's user-facing copy verbatim; repeating the literals is the point of the test.

The main window and the pulled-out Chat window each render their own shell and bind the same close-tab action id and content class; the shared literals are registry and layout names, not duplicated behaviour.
Deliberate cross-language parity: the page computes the desktop's fnv1a64 content revision in TypeScript, and both suites pin the same known values so the Rust and TS twins cannot drift apart.
